title: Funchal — Understand
body: Funchal is the capital of Madeira and home to almost half the island's population. The city climbs steeply from the harbour, and the difference between sea level and the upper suburbs is enough to change the weather. Unlike much of southern Europe the season here is inverted: the winter months are mild and green, and most attractions keep full hours all year.

title: Funchal — Get around
body: The old town, the cathedral and the market are all within a twenty minute walk of each other, and the seafront promenade runs several kilometres without a road crossing. Buses cover the suburbs cheaply. A car is a liability in the centre, where parking is scarce and the gradients are severe, but useful for the north of the island.

title: Santorini — Get around
body: Buses run from Fira to most villages in season but thin out considerably in winter, and the caldera villages are connected by stepped paths rather than roads. Most visitors hire a car or a quad. Out of season a number of the cliff-side hotels and restaurants close entirely, and the sunset crowds at Oia disappear.
